precepts.text: As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God. Shame on you if you come in here and sit on the talent God has given you. You have been given that gift for a reason: to utilize it and benefit your nation.
precepts.point: Nobody should be bogging down your talents and gifts; we should be accentuating those gifts, furthering them, and teaching others those talents where possible.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
Every member was set in the body for a reason, so Peter says: “As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.”

Shame on you if you come in here and sit on your hands, sit on the talent God has given you, and put forth no effort. If you have a craft or something to offer and you don't come in trying to show it and help, shame on you. You have been given that for a reason.

Your job is to utilize that gift and benefit your nation. Nobody should be bogging down your talents or making you stagnant; we should be accentuating those gifts, furthering them, and teaching them to others where possible. That is being a good steward: the gift is ministered one to another, so the whole body is built up.

precepts.text: As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God. The gift comes from the Lord, and it is used to minister one to another. You have not been given a gift just for you. If you only use it for yourself, it did not come from the Lord. These gifts are supposed to be utilized for the building of the body; that is the stewardship.
precepts.point: All these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will. God has divided to every man as he wanted. Everyone has received something. New brothers and sisters, you are trying to discover what the Lord wants you to do here, because you woke up in this time period for a reason. What are you bringing to the table? How are you going to benefit your people and carry this truth to the next level? Sisters, the same: this is not just about the brothers, it is about a nation.

note.label: Members of the Body  Pt2

precepts.why:
“But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal.” Everyone has a gift, but it goes toward the same goal in unison. It is not just for you. However the manifestation comes, there are different gifts given so that you can profit with all the nation.

Peter: “As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.” Where does the gift come from? The Lord. And what is it used for? To minister one to another.

You have not been given a gift just for you. If you have been given a gift and you only use it for yourself, it did not come from the Lord; it is not of the Lord. You are supposed to use that gift to benefit your nation and your people. That is why you were given it. If your gift only glorifies you, it is not about Christ; it is about you.

“as good stewards”: now you understand the stewardship program. These gifts are to be used for the building of the body, so that we can do what we need to do as a nation. The word of wisdom, the word of knowledge, faith, all given “to every man to profit withal.”

precepts.text: Let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer. But if any man suffer as a Christian, one that follows Christ and the commandments of God, let him not be ashamed.
precepts.point: That would be many of our sons and daughters who refuse to listen to their parents. If it isn't jail, it's a pregnancy, a disease, a marriage riddled with alcohol abuse and domestic violence. The parents in righteousness are supposed to oversee who their sons and daughters get hooked up with. That's why God gave children parents.

note.label: In a Game of Fools Without The Rules

precepts.why:
“For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil.” The rulers are a terror to those that do evil. Peter shows the difference between the two kinds of suffering: “But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men’s matters.” One of the titles for this class was going to be suffer not as a murderer.

“Yet if any man suffer as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God on this behalf.” Suffering as a Christian means suffering as one that follows Christ and the commandments of God, not Christianity. If we get locked up for doing what is right, and some of us will, we suffer that and glorify God.

The young man in the courtroom is suffering as a murderer, literally. He cannot say the Lord is going to repay them for what they are doing to him; the reason he is being judged is that he broke the laws of the Most High. He broke down crying because he is a wankster, not a gangster. Where are the homies and the shoot-em-up videos now? When you get locked up, nobody cares about your black ass once you are in jail. Esau is the devil for a reason; he lets the little negro run around with a gun killing his own people, and then he busts him, and he becomes property of the state, sweat equity for the prison system.

That is where many of our sons and daughters are going when they refuse to listen to their parents: if not jail, a pregnancy, a disease, a marriage riddled with alcohol abuse and domestic violence. That is why God gave children parents. We were not afraid of the power before; we broke the commandments, so the Lord put this beast over us, and when you mess up with him he has no pity. As they say in the islands, those who don’t hear will feel. Suffer, if you must, as a follower of Christ, never as an evildoer.

precepts.text: Forasmuch then as Christ hath suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves likewise with the same mind. If your mind is not prepared to suffer the same way Christ suffered, you are not a soldier in Christ. The Bible is telling you what is going to happen; do not live in la la land. For he that hath suffered in the flesh hath ceased from sin: that is how you become perfect. Those of you that want a comfortable life, this truth is not for you.
precepts.point: For the battle is not yours, but God's. Why does it say the battle belongs to the Lord? Because the Lord is always there fighting with you.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
Do not be afraid of armies and people; teach the word of God no matter what they threaten you with. You are not going to be a servant of God and have everything be good. You are not going to be a soldier in Christ and not suffer.

“Forasmuch then as Christ hath suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves likewise with the same mind”. The same way Christ suffered for us in the flesh, when the Romans crucified him, lynched him and beat him, you have to arm yourself with that same mind. If your mind is not ready to suffer the same way Christ suffered, you are not a soldier in Christ. The Bible is telling you what is going to happen, but some of you are in la-la land.

Eventually an army is going to surround my house, and they are going to lie on me and call me a terrorist or something stupid like that. I already know that is what they will do, so I prepare my mind. Federal agents are waiting to set you up. Do you think the American government is going to let us keep teaching and waking Israel up and just leave us alone? Read about COINTELPRO. Do you think that stopped? We are going up against a wicked, evil people who will put you away for the rest of your life and lie on you, knowing you did not do it, because of the teachings of Christ.

“for he that hath suffered in the flesh hath ceased from sin”. That is how you become perfect: you have to go through things and suffer in the flesh. Those of you who want a comfortable life, this truth is not for you. The battle is the Lord’s, and he fights with us, but we arm our minds to suffer as Christ did.

precepts.text: The end of all things is at hand: be ye therefore sober, and watch unto prayer, and above all things have fervent charity among yourselves.
precepts.point: Take ye heed, watch and pray, for ye know not when the time is. Stay ready.

note.label: Prepare Ye War

precepts.why:
Christ said to watch and pray, “for ye know not when the time is.” Peter says the same: “But the end of all things is at hand: be ye therefore sober, and watch unto prayer.” Be sober, man. Keep a clear mind.

“And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity shall cover the multitude of sins.” Fervent charity is the brotherly love we are supposed to have for one another, the way we are supposed to treat one another.

We need it because these things are taking place, and we see them taking place on the earth. The end of all things is at hand, so watching and praying goes together with a clear mind and with love among ourselves.

precepts.text: If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God, neither adding nor taking away.
precepts.point: From the beginning the Most High commanded the prophets to speak his words and diminish not a word: do not be afraid to tell the nations what the scripture actually says, that salvation is to Israel and that there is no female deity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God”. To speak as the oracles of God is to speak neither adding nor taking away, only what the Most High has said.

New brothers in this truth should not rush to debate before they have studied to shew themselves approved; uttering things that are not in the scriptures is not a good look. Speak as the oracles of God, “that God in all things may be glorified through Jesus Christ”.

precepts.text: Think it not strange concerning the fiery trial; rejoice as partakers of Christ's suffering.
precepts.point: Just as grandchildren crown the old, we glorify our Father in heaven and our forefathers by our repentance and return to righteousness.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but the Lord trieth the hearts.” The fining pot and the furnace remove impurities from silver and gold; likewise the Most High tries our hearts through trials to rid us of our impurities.

“Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you.” The fiery trial is not a strange thing; it is the furnace, and we rejoice as partakers of Christ’s suffering.

We must go through trials and tribulations to gain the kingdom. This is why Christianity is false when it teaches you only have to accept Jesus in your heart to be saved forever. That is not what the scriptures say.

precepts.text: If any man suffer as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but glorify God on this behalf.
precepts.point: The disciples were called Christians first in Antioch, and those disciples were Jews. Christians were not all nations or races as men think today; the Greek word Christianos comes from Christos, the anointed one, so a Christian is a kinsman of the Messiah and a follower of Christ, an anointed one.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“Yet if any man suffer as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God on this behalf.”

Peter wrote this to Israel scattered abroad. A Christian is a follower of Christ, a kinsman of the Messiah, and to suffer as one is no shame but a reason to glorify God. That is the name the disciples, who were Jews, were first called in Antioch.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 12 Red Dragon, Red Herring

precepts.why: We close out here. “If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye”: if we are reproached for being in this truth we are supposed to rejoice. “But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer”: don’t say I’m being reproached for Christ when you’re in jail because you are a thief; the law says thou shalt not steal. If you are a pedophile, we are coming down on you with both feet; we are not going to support that. “Or as a busybody in other men’s matters”: don’t suffer for being nosy. “Yet if any man suffer as a Christian, let him not be ashamed”: don’t be ashamed for being reproached for being God’s anointed. “For the time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God”: we are the house of God, so we expect tribulation to come. “And if the righteous scarcely be saved”: that goes with “they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony.” “Commit the keeping of their souls to him in well doing”: which means keeping the commandments.
